result.note: Tests what an intensive revision involves, where the SIR was postponed, and the court and phase details of the February 2026 challenge.

questions.prompt: In early 2026, the Election Commission of India drew criticism for postponing its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls in one poll-bound state while going ahead in others. In which state was the exercise postponed?
questions.explain: The ECI postponed the SIR in BJP-ruled Assam but went ahead in opposition-held West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, plus Puducherry. The SIR was initially slated for the states heading to the polls in 2026.
questions.source: However, eyebrows were raised when the ECI postponed the exercise in BJP-ruled Assam while going forward in opposition-held West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala (plus Puducherry where the BJP is in an alliance with the government).

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls, as of February 2026:
items: Unlike annual reviews, an intensive revision requires every voter to be re-verified.
West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee challenged the SIR by arguing before the Calcutta High Court.
Phase 2 of the SIR includes Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Mamata Banerjee personally argued in the Supreme Court, not a High Court, on 4 February 2026 to halt the SIR. An intensive revision re-verifies every voter and often demands fresh documentation, and Phase 2 now covers BJP strongholds such as UP and Gujarat.
questions.source: Unlike annual reviews, an intensive revision requires every single voter to be re-verified, often demanding fresh documentation.
